It looks like a way to replicate this would be
- load /latest - do not scroll down
- wait for new articles to be published (20-30 minutes is probably enough for DEV.to, basically wait for new articles to have been published) - in test you can create articles to suit your needs.
- scroll down until a request to /search/feed_content?... is made (which returns a json list of articles)
- observe the placement of the new items in the existing list (you can view the search response and text search by title on the page) 

I'm definitely able to replicate this behavior (new items appear out of order in the latest feed when scrolling). 

I think there are a few strategies that could be followed, I'm not sure any of them are obviously correct without drawbacks

- backfilling articles items to their appropriate location in the list when they're loaded from the paged request (if an article is earlier than the displayed region - it's inserted in the page you've already scrolled past) - this could cause new articles to be placed out of view (it's unlikely someone would scroll backward looking for changes often). 
- sending a "earlier than" mark based on the last article (oldest we already have) rather than a page number - this would prevent newer items (published since the page was loaded) from appearing at all, but should be easier to keep items in order. This is a change to limit what articles we request/retrieve to avoid the issue.
- accept the current state of things, that sometimes this gives a confusing result in what normally looked like a sorted list

I think there might be two aspects to this bug. The one that you mention @djuber, but I think there's also something else funky going on... As far as I know, the expectation is that the UI should present posts in the order they're received in the API response, but once we start scrolling, that isn't always happening.

You can reproduce in DEV fairly reliably by

- visiting /latest
- immediately start scrolling
- eventually (for me it's after I start hitting posts from 2 hours ago-ish) you'll see something like the screenshot in the description above
- when I inspect the network requests the "out of place" article was actually sent from the API to appear between posts of a similar published time. For some reason it's being inserted into the UI in a much later position.

I'd need to investigate further but my initial suspicion is there might be a timing issue occurring where multiple pages of posts are loaded in quick succession and the individual callbacks to update the UI are overlapping each other.
@cmgorton @aitchiss I would love to work on this issue, could you please assign this to me? thanks!

@aitchiss @djuber Today I did some testing and discovered a strange recurrence for this bug.
The bug always seems to happen at the 51st position (the first 50 cards are fine).

When new articles are being added by other users, the card will stay at that exact position and other cards will pass by.
After the card has been there for X amount of time (my guess is when 50 cards have passed, and therefore it has found its right position) it will move on with other cards in the normal flow.

![1634653623_1920x937](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42511917/137942337-04e10049-cc8f-4834-8bbc-aabf705c7879.png)

![1634662256_950x464](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42511917/137956190-9191d047-3a8e-4979-a5e0-e4625968363c.png)

After like 30 seconds of taking the @SGGregory 's screenshot above I received a notification (since I have subbed to her), that says that the post is made *a day ago*.

![1634661150_1068x369](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42511917/137954158-3ea1974c-61af-4437-8212-661e3d7a1556.png)

It should have said the post had been published *a minute ago*.

Could all these indexing issues be derived from faulty timestamps or something?
